subject: Renewal pricing reauthorization & staircase commit offer
messages:
From: Lena Hoffmann <lena@stellaretail.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Renewal: pricing + additional capacity ask

Hi Rachel,

Were coming up on our renewal and wanted to open a conversation about price stability and a modest capacity increase. Q1 usage exceeded our forecast (see attached brief) and the board wants certainty on unit economics if we commit for the next 12 months.

Specifically: 1) can we get a 6 month price-hold on current per-token rates if we sign a 12 month commitment, 2) is there a structured credit or step-down discount available for the first two quarters if usage spikes, and 3) we need an additional 20% burst pool for holiday season traffic (one-time uplift).

We have procurement on copy. Happy to hop on a 30 minute sync this week to run through options.

Thanks,
Lena
Lena Hoffmann
VP, Platform & Data
Stellar Retail

Attachment: usage_report_q1.csv (CSV summary, 3 pages)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Hoffmann <lena@stellaretail.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@stellaretail.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal: pricing + additional capacity ask

Hi Lena,

Thanks for the context and the usage snapshot. Appreciate the specificity  that helps. We can absolutely structure something that balances price stability with predictable economics on our side.

High-level proposal before a call:
- 12 month committed volume with a 6-month price-hold on current token rate (locks retail rates for months 1-6)
- Staircase commit: a two-step commit ramp (base commit + an optional accelerated tranche) with a forgiveness credit if quarter-over-quarter usage >25% (one-time spike credit up to 10% of that quarter's overage)
- One-time sprint/burst pool: +20% reserved burst for the seasonal window, billed monthly but only consumed if used; early-burn credits available if they exceed forecast

Ill loop in CS and Sales Ops and put together a term sheet (v2) with numbers for your review. Are you available Wed 3/4 or Thu 3/5 for a 30 min call?

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

---

Subject: Internal: Pricing parameters & legal checks for Stellar Retail renewal

Team,

Quick internal note following Lenas ask. Key constraints: 6mo price-hold, spike forgiveness credit, +20% burst pool. Proposed structure attached as term sheet (draft). Need:
- Ben: a commercial proposal with clear per-token rates, blended discount tiers, and the one-time burst billing approach. Keep net revenue protected (min commit floor) and include an optional acceleration tranche.
- Monica (CS): confirm operational feasibility for the burst pool (routing, pre-warm, capacity SLOs) and whether we can guarantee burst availability within SLA window.
- Markus (Legal/Finance): confirm if price-hold + forgiveness credit is acceptable from a revenue recognition and contract amendment perspective. Any redline bullets we should expect?

Im aiming to send their draft v2 by EOD Friday so we can review before the 3/10 call. Attaching my working draft: Stellar_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v1.pdf (internal).

Thanks,
Rachel

Attachment: Stellar_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v1.pdf (internal draft)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-04T14:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Internal: Pricing parameters & legal checks for Stellar Retail renewal

Rachel, team,

On the commercial front I recommend:
- Base commit: 12 months at a 15% discount to public list rates, annualized; this provides the revenue floor.
- Acceleration tranche: optional +30% commit at 10% incremental discount if signed within 30 days of the amendment.
- Price-hold: lock current effective per-token rate for months 1-6 capped at current net after the 15% discount. After month 6 rates revert to the stepped schedule in the term sheet.
- Spike forgiveness credit: if any monthly consumption exceeds forecast by >25%, apply a one-time credit equal to 8% of the overage invoice for that month (credit applied to next invoice).
- Burst pool charge: bill the 20% reserved capacity at a discounted reserve rate (50% of on-demand burst), actual consumption billed at standard overage pricing but credits apply per the forgiveness clause.

Ive attached a pricing appendix with numeric illustrations and an example invoice. If Monica can confirm burst feasibility were good to present a clean v2 to Lena.

Cheers,
Ben

Attachment: pricing_appendix_stellar_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, illustrative)

From: Lena Hoffmann <lena@stellaretail.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@stellaretail.com>
Date: 2026-03-10T14:23:00Z
Subject: Re: Renewal: pricing + additional capacity ask

Thanks Rachel and Ben for the quick turnaround. The framework looks promising. A few clarifications from procurement/legal before we can sign:
1) We like the 6-month price-hold but would prefer language that guarantees any downstream model-variant changes during hold do not increase unit cost (i.e., equivalent SKU parity).
2) Forgiveness credit: can the credit be applied retroactively to the month where the overage occurred rather than next invoice? That helps our month-end reconciliation.
3) Burst pool: we will sign the reserve, but can we request a short-term increase to 25% for the upcoming promotion window if forecast shows a higher spike?

Ive attached a redlined term sheet (Stellar_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf) with inline comments. If you can accept the three bullets above were ready to route to final approvals.

Best,
Lena
Procurement Team

Attachment: Stellar_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v2.pdf (redlines)

Date: 2026-03-15T16:42:00Z
Subject: Final: Stellar renewal - accepted edits and next steps (DocuSign)

Hi Lena,

Thanks for the redlines  we reviewed them with Legal and CS. Short answers below and summary of changes in the attached final term sheet:

1) Model-variant parity during price-hold: Accepted. Weve added a clause that model-substitutions that are materially similar (performance and footprint) will be mapped to the equivalent SKU rate for the 6-month hold period. That prevents accidental unit-cost drift.
2) Forgiveness credit timing: We can apply the credit retroactively to the overage invoice as a bill adjustment (notated on that months invoice), provided the claim is submitted within 14 days of the invoice date.
3) Burst pool flexibility: We can accommodate a one-time temporary increase to 25% for the promotional window, subject to 7 days notice so CS can pre-warm and route capacity. That increase will be billed under the same reserve/consumption rules noted earlier.

Attached: Stellar_Renewal_Term_Sheet_v3_Final.pdf (incorporates edits) and a one-page summary. DocuSign link: https://app.redwood.com/docusign/abcd-efgh-2026.

Next steps:
- Lena: sign the DocuSign (procurement) or let us know minor edits within 48 hours.
- Monica: Ive asked CS to provision burst reservation and add a runbook for the promotional window; please confirm by EOD 3/18.
- Markus: please prepare the amendment for countersignature (Ill route upon Lenas signature).

Appreciate the partnership here. If all good Ill schedule the kickoff for capacity runbook and billing handoff.

Best regards,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
